style_when: the article is a purely conceptual synthesis or policy dilemma where no physical facility, machine, or supply chain exists, and an elegant abstract paper silhouette states the idea. Never reach for paper collage when the story describes physical manufacturing, freight, energy, hardware, or heavy infrastructure — use cinematic still or telephoto industry instead
prompt: Minimalist editorial cut-paper collage arranged on the dark console desk of a control room. A lowered checkpoint barrier arm of safety-yellow and graphite striped paper crosses the left third of the frame, its tip pinning one bone-white computer punch card mid-pass; a short queue of identical punch cards with clipped corners waits behind the arm. Hand-torn rag paper with visible fibre, halftone newsprint texture on the dark shapes, crisp cut edges, physical cast shadows under every layer. One raking light from the left throwing long soft shadows. Muted palette of bone white, graphite and safety yellow, generous empty margin on the right, no people, no legible print.
rationale: This is a purely conceptual software-architecture story with no physical facility to photograph, so an editorial cut-paper collage states the mechanism cleanly. The article's own noun — the gate that catches calls before they run — becomes a striped barrier pinning a program card, legible at card size and in the site's palette. It also rotates the desk back to an illustrative medium after four photographic flux headers.
cue: a deterministic gate in program logic
subject: a striped barrier gate pinning a computer punch card of a shell command
core_thesis: An ungated agent executes its worst calls harmfully at a 74.83% rate, and the cheapest fix is a deterministic gate in program logic that checks every action before it runs — not a bigger model.
core_conflict: Unchecked execution speed versus pre-execution verification: the agent's proposal fires before anything verifies it, and a 0.34 ms code-level gate must stand between the model's call and the tool.
composition: asymmetric low horizontal composition with the striped gate arm crossing the left third, its tip pinning one caught card, a short card queue behind it, and large empty rag-paper margin on the right
